steps.name: Proprietor
steps.text: Hey, don't go anywhere.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: You've fooled me once already. What am I going to stay for?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Mr. Ruan might not be any giant of the ages, but it is his absolute, exact control of his brush's weight that makes him one of the most lauded out there.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: This painting shows the study of Mr. Ruan's energy, and has attained three, perhaps four-tenths of it, but the strokes are crooked. The bodies fray from the form, and the form makes no attempt to adjoin. You have a sense of humor to tout this as a genuine work, don't you?

steps.name: Proprietor
steps.text: Just hold it, hold it, okay!

steps.name: Proprietor
steps.text: I didn't lay out the whole, unbearable truth because I knew you'd hate hearing it... but this really is a genuine article of his!

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Unbearable truth? He lives in this city. He's a fellow man of yours. You would slander him like that?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Not to mention, no matter how unbearable things are, he wouldn't produce a work this shoddy.

steps.name: Proprietor
steps.text: His sight has gone.

steps.name: Proprietor
steps.text: I am absolutely not lying about this! The painting I possess here is a consequence of Mr. Ruan going blind!

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Mr. Ruan was frequently ill in his youth, that I've heard.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: But being so prideful in spirit, how could anything, even going blind, have him let this sort of thing out into the realm, to ruin his own fame?

steps.name: Proprietor
steps.text: Just... listen to me.

steps.name: Proprietor
steps.text: Mr. Ruan's eye disease kept getting worse and worse in recent years, to the point he could take ever so slightly small print, put it up against his face, and he couldn't make it out.

steps.name: Proprietor
steps.text: He'd rather have died than admit he can't see, precisely because of his pride.

spans.text: He'd rather have died than admit he can't see, precisely

steps.name: Proprietor
steps.text: There was a scoundrel who found out as such, played coy around him, tricked their way into his good favors, and then shoved some finely crafted contract before him and goaded him into signing.

steps.name: Proprietor
steps.text: And just like that, not only is Mr. Ruan in massive debt, even knowledge of his eye disease is getting out.

steps.name: Proprietor
steps.text: He's been ill for several months since then. Some say he's gone completely blind.

spans.text: He's been ill for several months since then. Some say he's gone

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: ...Is the human soul truly that venomous?

steps.name: Proprietor
steps.text: So it goes.

steps.name: Proprietor
steps.text: Here, if that was as far as it went, and he'd simply fallen for some swindler's scheme, I wouldn't be throwing around the word 'unbearable.'

steps.name: Proprietor
steps.text: But he's been ruined ever since then, forced to the worst ends to meet his debt.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: The worst ends?

steps.name: Proprietor
steps.text: His painting has lost all value since going blind. The experts won't give him a second look. He even started going by the 'blind painter' circus act, soliciting the wealthy here to watch him paint, in exchange for their charity.

steps.name: Proprietor
steps.text: To be fully honest, nothing he paints now goes for much of anything—not any more than what those socialites tip him, even. This painting I have here now was procured from one of those—

spans.text: To be fully honest, nothing he paints now goes for much of anything—not any more than what those socialites tip him, even. This painting I have here now was procured

steps.name: Proprietor
steps.text: Eh? Where'd you go?

steps.name: Wealthy Person
steps.text: A colorful character you are, old Ruan, small enough you look amazingly like my grandson here! And this light ink on your head, it's not so far off the birthmark on my grandson's! Are you really blind, sir?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: ...I am.

steps.name: Wealthy Person
steps.text: I suppose as much. How would you miss even the big bold print on that contract if you weren't? Hahah.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: ...Hah.

steps.name: Wealthy Person
steps.text: Here's your painter's pay, and I do bid you accept. Farewell for now.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: So the proprietor was not wrong. The state of Mr. Ruan truly is unbearable.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Who's that?!

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: A storyteller, no more.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: A storyteller..?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: I merely know that Mr. Ruan is a prideful one, who would pursue utmost realism in better years, who would fixate on scenery for days on end. Yet I didn't know he would resign himself now as a peacockerel within the cage, a sideshow of a beast.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: If you're a sharer of the passion here to give me a wake-up call, I appreciate your kindness.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: But ambitions are one's own. I'm blind in both eyes, unable to tell any longer what's fake and what's real. I'm simply struggling in my swansong. It beats falling dead on the roadside, that's all.

steps.name: Speculator
steps.text: Ruan, old Ruan!

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Who are you...?

steps.name: Speculator
steps.text: I'm the one that came to see you for a painting a few days ago. Did you forget so fast?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Mr... Chu, I presume.

steps.name: Speculator
steps.text: Yes, that's me!

steps.name: Speculator
steps.text: What under Heaven is this 'Scene of Flower Plumage' you painted?

steps.name: Speculator
steps.text: The fowlbeast's feet look like they're in pieces, and the coloring on these petals is turbid at best! You may well have flipped your palette straight onto the canvas!

steps.name: Speculator
steps.text: I showed what you drew to some experts and asked them what technique this was, how your consciousness of form held, and can you guess what they said?

steps.name: Speculator
steps.text: They said any 'form-conscious' part of you had long devolved into 'bone-obsequious!' Everything you paint wobbles and warps! When was the last time you laid a single firm line?!

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Bone-obsequious?!

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Mr. Chu, we agreed at the start that you'd pay as you saw fit, that any amount would be fine as long as you didn't regret it afterwards.

steps.name: Speculator
steps.text: If I knew this was how you ended up, then forget painter's pay, you wouldn't pay me to take your works! If you don't refund me today, I'll go to the authorities and tell them you're passing off shoddy goods!

spans.text: If I knew this was how you ended up, then forget painter's pay, you wouldn't pay
to take your works! If you don't refund me today, I'll go to the authorities and tell them you're passing off shoddy goods!

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Mr. Chu, in light of the fact you made your agreement, the authorities would not pay mind.

spans.text: Mr. Chu, in light of the fact you
your agreement, the authorities would not pay mind.

steps.name: Speculator
steps.text: Does this have anything to do with you?

steps.name: Speculator
steps.text: If the mandarins won't listen, I have other ways. No matter what, this geriatric's going to cough up my money!

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: If you try your 'other ways,' that will be cause to trouble the authorities.

spans.text: will be cause to trouble the authorities.

steps.name: Speculator
steps.text: You—?!

steps.name: Speculator
steps.text: Hmph. Fine, I'll swallow this loss.
The visitor lifts up the painting, asserts himself, and viciously begins to tear.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: What are you doing?!
Throwing all his strength into his hands, he tears the painting into shreds in but a few short motions.
He tosses them up into the air, the scraps falling down like snow, all over Mr. Ruan.

steps.name: Speculator
steps.text: Ruan, even beggars would be ashamed to act the way you do! They were right, you're bone-obsequious! Utterly depraved!

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Me... obsequious? Depraved?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Said as such, no, I cannot refute him.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: No, no!

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: 'No?'

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: You keep on repeating how you're blind, but are you truly, fully sightless?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Playing the jester for coin is unbearable enough as is, but still you have to feign some for your comedic act. And you have the conscience to speak the word 'no?'

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: This... What do you mean?!

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: I need not mention the infant's birthmark. Further, you made a cry before that Chu fellow actually began to tear up your painting.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: If my guess is correct, your sight is largely gone. The written word is a lost cause, and you can hardly even tell light shades from dark, hence the total suffering of your brushwork.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: But full blindness? There sits a subtle lie.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Sir... you are observant.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Where are you going?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: With even this final lie dead, what grants me any standing to cling to life?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: I may as well find a quiet place... and be done with it all. It'll be clean!

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Clean?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: With your death, Mr. Ruan henceforth will be immortalized as the bone-obsequious, utterly depraved man. What of that do you call clean?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: But what else ought I do? What else can I do?

spans.text: But what else ought I do? What else

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Full sightlessness or not aside, even if you are blind, does that render you unable to paint?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Render me... unable to paint?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: I can... perhaps I can...

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: —Forgive my dullness! I ask you impart your teachings upon this blinded painter's method!

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: That which I have heard is not as you have heard; which I have touched is not as you have touched; which I have tasted is not as you have tasted. To what end would I teach you?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Heard... touched... tasted?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Hm.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: I am tired for today. Fare well by yourself.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Sir?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: I must have misheard—

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Do you refer to me?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: I imagined we should have nothing left to talk about.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: I'd be remiss! Your great grace will ever be engraved on my heart!

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Hmph, interesting.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: What grace have I done you?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: You imparted upon me the painting style of sound, touch and taste, for which I was finally in these months able to paint a steadfast work.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Truth be told, I was planning to invite my fellow artists to judge my new work, but didn't expect to meet you here. Now I think of it, you should be the first to appraise my painting, sir.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: That need not happen.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: What I'd like to know is, what is it that you've heard, that you've touched, that you've tasted?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: After you left that day, I pondered carefully at how the wealthy man jeered at me, how the merchant berated me, how you advised me...

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: I may not see clearly, but to put the forms and expressions that I hear onto paper, though it may not be so easy, was in the end a followable path.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Then how would I, as you hear me, appear within your painting?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: You'd be lean and tall, an aloof man of middle age, faintly bearded, eyes lively and flickering.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: This counts for little. You still hold onto some vision. To gauge my figure and silhouette would not be hard.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: That said, should I shut my eyes and listen carefully, you occasionally seem too like a woman of cold face and warm heart...

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Ahem.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: I blurted that out. Don't mind it.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: I don't, I don't. Or rather, I have a mind for how amusing it is.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Then what of touch? And taste?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Touch is the simplest of all. What I want to draw, I toy with in my hands, carefully feeling all around it.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: That which is too large, I can simply move my desk to the side, and feel, think and draw alternately.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: As for taste... it's funny to say, but I've given the flavors of ink cakes and paints a sample.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Knowing only a single paint's flavor isn't enough. I've mixed paints according to my previous experiences painting, had someone compare, and once the color was a perfect match, I took a few drops into my mouth, and committed the flavor to heart.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: You... do not fear poisoning yourself?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: To pick up the brush once again is my blessing as great as Heaven. The poison of a drop of paint is little to fear.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Enough. Knowing you've strived so greatly, the painting is bound not to fall short.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: I'll disturb you no longer. Go.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Were you... waiting for me all this time here, sir?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Not exactly.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: I was simply whiling time away on this street, saw you coming from afar, face pale, and came to greet you.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: What happened?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: My fellow artists pointed out many a shortcoming in this painting of mine... no more.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: No more?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: This was your first earnest painting since going blind. It's only natural it should hold shortcomings. Why so downcast all of a sudden?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Trifles, just... trifles.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: You needn't concern yourself for me, sir, I'll... be going home.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Second-rate.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: That much is right.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: And incisive!

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Of course a second-rate man would set his brush to a second-rate work, haha, hahah!

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Hahah... hahaha...

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: So why is this painting second-rate?! What part of it is? How many years do you want my half-blind self slaving to see it?!

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Forget it... My bone-obsequious self's impossible to shake now.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: I'm worn, I'm tired. All good things come to an end. This was long overdue.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: I just hate to let down that good sir... but I'm at the end of my rope.
The painter, eyes clouded, raises his head and looks to the ceiling rafters.
By his desk are the several bolts of tough silk that he resolved to purchase months ago.
After he finished painting, before setting out, he imagined scenes of all kinds. Warm ones, ice-cold ones, ones that would make one blush with shame.

The one scene he didn't imagine was that they would look at his painting, then look at him, and fall silent for a good while, before one among them—whoever it was—indifferently muttered the words 'second-rate.'
The others seemed to feel that excessive, and began to make addendum to those two words. However, after they'd finished doing so, not one of them had actually dissented to those two words.

spans.text: The others seemed to feel that excessive, and began to make addendum to those two words. However, after they'd finished doing so, not one of them had actually dissented to

steps.text: And now, no longer does he see a need to paint anything on these silks.
The painter stands up, and throws one silk bolt to the rafters.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Mr. Ruan, I'd thought you were full of prospects. What are you doing here, still, seeking death after all?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Sir, what do you intend now by visiting me?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Whether a painting is good or bad should, first and foremost, be for its painter to appraise, shouldn't it?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: I know you mean to encourage me, sir, but at this time, I can't hear anything but mockery in it.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Mockery?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Mr. Ruan, I merely ask you one question. Do you want to see how exactly the painting you made turned out, or not?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: I'm tired. Don't let me keep you, sir.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Tell me.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: How could I not want to?!

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Then that makes things easier.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Simply listen to me, and this evening after the Hour of Yu, before tomorrow morning at the Hour of Ch'en, you will be sure to see clearly and think clearly.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: I'm endlessly thankful for your kindness, sir. But while this staving off may save me for a time, it won't save me for the rest of it.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: If the Hour of Yu comes, and all I see is still an impression, what will you do then?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: These eyes of mine ail at their core. I've tried remedies one and all, none of which were any use. And you can restore my sight with a simple utterance? Can something so fine be true?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Do you think I'm some sage doctor?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Let me tell you this. If you truly want to see clearly tonight, then come the Hour of Ch'en tomorrow, you will lose all sight, all of it. It won't be an impression, it will be jet-black.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Is that... the solemn truth?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: True and false are for you and you alone to determine.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: If you're willing, you can go to bed right now, and you will naturally wake at the Hour of Yu. After the sun breaks at the end of night, at tomorrow's Hour of Ch'en, you will be cut off from light altogether.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: If you're unwilling, then simply do not sleep. Sit at home doing nothing, or go out and bide your time. Either way, your eyes will not be getting better.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: This... this is so sudden. If you could explain a little more thoroughly, sir...

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: There's nothing to explain. Sleep if you like to, wake if you like to. It's not as if anyone can tell you what to do.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Think it over by yourself.
The painter gazes to the white bolt of fabric fluttering in the rafters, then looks back at the scroll upon his desk, and adds no words more to the air.
He simply takes off his shoes, lies down on his couch fully clothed, and quickly falls asleep.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Once you regain your eyesight, and see your painting, you'll understand that it was not you that was lowly, but the prejudice living among them.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: After that... peruse well.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Peruse books, peruse paintings, peruse the scenery tonight.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Even in a city this small, seeing it all in just a single short night is far too much of a rush.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: A single short night—perhaps too short to finish even a dream.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: For you, and for me, it's just too rushed.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: It's gotten late, and I don't want to waste a moment.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: I don't want to waste a moment, but it has... gotten late, after all.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: It's—

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: It's the Hour of Yu, I'm sure, right now is the Hour of Yu!
The painter springs up from the couch, rushes to his desk, and opens the painting scroll ridiculed as second-rate, burning to see it and take it in.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: This line here is crooked, this expression here is oblique, this coloring here is somewhat gaudy—

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: But these are all things you could fairly point out without hesitation.Why would they call this painting 'second-rate?'

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: This painting is about on par with the works from my auspicious twenties. How is it second-rate?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: I'm going to find them and discuss—

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: No!

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: I only have tonight... I only have tonight!
The sun dusks, the room dim and waning, but in the painter's eyes, every lamp shines bright as the sun, so dazzling he can barely keep his eyes open.
The gold, glistering light stabs to the point he drips with tears.
How he would love once again in this light to take in his own paintings, and his treasured masterpieces, gaze at the beautiful scenery and the common masses beyond the edges of the canvas.
But he only has tonight.
He drags the silk bolt down off the rafters, pulls off a length and mounts it on his board, and in a frenzy cleans his brushes, grinds his ink, and mixes his paints.
He lifts his fine brush, and before he's even thought about what to paint, his hand so accustomed to linework involuntarily begins to move.
Just as how hounded by the night that chases relentlessly, man will involuntarily desire to flee.
Just as how on seeing the madder sun that sinks gently, man will involuntarily desire to give chase.
Following contours and forming likenesses, he suddenly remembers an absurd story he heard long ago.
As night fell, a man chased the setting sun, running without stop.
He ran until his sweat rained down, until he'd drunk a stream dry, a lake dry, a great river dry.
But he still continued to run without stop.
Because he only had tonight.
The painter becomes aware of the parched sensation in his mouth, and picks up the brush-cleaning bowl by his side.
The water within is mixed with the ink from the brushes, one muddy mess by now.
He stares at this black water for a moment, then drinks it dry in one gulp, and after that thinks about nothing else.
He only has tonight.
The east is bright.
If the painter so cared, he would surely notice the storyteller's figure hidden in the shadows all along, gazing at him blankly, daring not even to breathe loudly, having watched the entire night.
But he long since had no mind to care.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: I've... finished.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: I've painted...
Upon the fabric meticulously ink-washed and detailed again and again, there in the painting is Mr. Ruan reclining by his desk, gazing out of the window and to far away.
What lies there?
Looking at the eyes of the Mr. Ruan within the painting, the Mr. Ruan outside knows. There is every light he has ever seen, from his birth to this very moment.
He carefully picks up the completed painting, and relying on his familiarity with the arrangement of his room, ventures forth a step—

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Careful not to knock anything over.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: Sir?!

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: I'll go and hang the painting for you.

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: That friend of mine lives right here. You don't need to take me any further now, sir.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: You're sure you can rely on him?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: If even he can't be depended on... then there's no one in this entire city I can trust anymore.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Mr. Ruan, this work of yours can be said to have both body and soul, to be a pinnacle of an achievement. Will you only be content if there are truly others to nod their approval?

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: (Chuckle)

steps.name: Mr. Ruan
steps.text: In the end, I just can't get away from my bone-obsequious self.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: (Mutter) Even now... bone-obsequious?

steps.name: Male Voice
steps.text: Mr. Ruan, what's wrong with—

steps.name: Male Voice
steps.text: Help! Someone's thrown up blood and fainted!

steps.name: Female Voice
steps.text: Ah Qi, run to the clinic and fetch a doctor!

steps.name: Female Voice
steps.text: What did you do to him? What happened to him?

steps.name: Male Voice
steps.text: I didn't do anything! All I did was say a few words!

steps.name: Female Voice
steps.text: What did you say?

steps.name: Male Voice
steps.text: His character was unbearable, and no matter how realistic his painting was, it would never be brilliant, not to mention the fact it was a self-portrait, which practically screamed him blowing his own horn...

steps.name: Male Voice
steps.text: I'd just invited Mr. Zhang from the city's painting circles over, and that's what he quietly told me before he left.

steps.name: Female Voice
steps.text: Well, at least Mr. Zhang knew to be quiet! And you said all that straight to him?!

steps.name: Male Voice
steps.text: No! I was just thinking about it—how could I tell him any of that?! I only said, his painting was...

steps.name: Male Voice
steps.text: The very top of the... bottom end.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: The very top of the bottom end?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Oh, okay, great, fine, the very very top of the bottom!

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Not like anyone even needs to care about this stupid city.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: How can a being from my brush be so malicious?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Forget it. You're not really malicious, you just have more on your mind than the Biteys. The real scary sight is someone who hasn't slept properly.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: I'll just call you 'Envy.'

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Now go!
The newly named Ink Spirit wriggles its body, turns around and heads over to the back.
The Biteys and Angrys huddled there appear duly fearful, and scatter in a snap like smoke.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Footsteps?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: (Mutter) The old bastard's in way too much of a hurry...

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: (Mutter) I was just adding a few more strokes inside my own painting. Is anything ever not of interest to...?

spans.text: (Mutter) I was just adding a few more strokes inside my own painting. Is anything ever

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: Sir?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: No, wait, you're not the old bastard—

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: You're... Mr. Ruan?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: It's been over twenty years. You're still alive?

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: Much thanks to your blessing, I'm technically still alive for now.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Take a seat.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: I'll be fine.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: The mountain rock's ice-cold, and the air's frigid and thick. These old bones of mine won't hold up to much flailing.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Mountain rock?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: (Mutter) Right, he's totally blind. Of course he couldn't see it...

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: (Mutter) So how exactly... did he get inside my painting?

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: Am I interrupting?

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: Were you talking about something important? Did I eavesdrop?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: No, no.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: I'm just curious. How have you pulled through, over these past twenty years?

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: It's a funny story, come to mention.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: That day, after I woke up in hospital, the doctor said I'd practically ended up half-dead, and that I absolutely needed to recover my presence of mind, and was never to get angry again.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: I felt disheartened myself, anyway. I abandoned my fame, gave up on painting, sold off all my property, refunded that one sum of money, and left the city.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: Even that painting I'd spilled my blood, sweat and tears over, I sold at the lowest price to someone else.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: In my heart at the time, I thought, wherever I ended up, that'd be where my bones would lie.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: In that regard, I shouldn't have interfered so much back then. You would've been better off if I left you alone.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: You needn't feel apologetic, sir.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: When did I apologize to you again?

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: You try to cover it, but the art of listening you imparted on me back then, I've never once let slip in the years since.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: *cough* Ahem.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: After I left, I quickly ran out of travel funds, but I wasn't six feet under quite yet. It pains me to say, but I had to take up the brush once again.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: Only, this time I don't seek out any noble or the like anymore. As long as I sit in the street with my canvas and brush, people will naturally come to me for still life portraits.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: And you're still the 'blind painter?'

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: Haha. The painter may truly be blind now, but those requesting paintings may not necessarily see it, that's all.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: You don't tell them?

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: If they're satisfied with what I paint, that's good enough. What does it matter if the painter's blind or not, really.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: People often think I paint well, and want me to draw something dead and lifeless like their courtyard, and all I can do is confess my blindness at that point, and give them a fright.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: So it sounds to me like their praise still inflates you with pride?

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: You've asked me so many questions, sir, but that one is the best.
The mountain winds blow through, a light rustling from the room's furnishings in response.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: Do you remember that funny term, 'bone-obsequious?'

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: I'll never forget it.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: I sought others' recognition by every means I could back then, as if I wouldn't survive without the nod from them. My mind to flatter seeped into my bones. They nailed me with those two very words, 'bone-obsequious.' It left me tossing and turning at night.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: But only afterwards, once I'd left home, and that narrow little patch of world, did I find that it was far from just me. Everyone's either looking to please or be pleased.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: Is there truly anyone who'll take it all in stride? Maybe. But I haven't met them.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: Your life starts in infancy following everything your parents say, then comes youth and bowing down to your sweetheart, then you're swept up in the prime of your life trying to cater yourself to the current style, and once you're old, you might well still be going gentle as you can on your children.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: We please and please and please, but we only do it so those we worry about give us their recognition, and that recognition's only for our own self-comfort.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: I've not a care now. When I'm flattered, yes, I'm tickled pink. When I'm berated, yes, I'm the most ashamed in the land.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: But after a nap, I feel easy again, and what others say crosses my eyes and vanishes like smoke.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: At this point, only my heart's left carrying on my old bone-obsequious self. Just the heart.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: A great swig of wine should've followed hearing your piece.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Only at these times do I think it's a shame that sister of mine isn't here.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: I have nothing to give in return after hearing your cautionary tale.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Let me show you out.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: No rush, no rush.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: Besides, you did me that kindness after all, sir. How could I have the nerve to be taking a present from you?

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: There seems to be some sound coming from your side.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: It's like the wind blowing a painting scroll, yet like an animal's movements, yet with some of your own feelings too.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: I couldn't repay you for your great grace back then, no matter how. Let me at least draw a portrait of this being, and gift it to you? How would you feel about that, sir?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Go ahead.
The painter makes a few scarce strokes, the technique neither the meticulous, nor the freehand kind.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: How's my painting?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Alike. Extremely alike.

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: Haha! Good, that's good!

steps.name: Guest
steps.text: You don't need to see me off too far, I'll be on my way now.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: How many remain out there who can enter and leave my paintings as freely as him? He... couldn't even see anything.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: So long as the realm still holds characters like him, who'd want to sleep, and who'd want to wake up?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: I was thinking I'd choose a good day out of the next few to get some proper sleep, but now...
Upon her desk, the painter's parchment, brushed with rough ink a moment before, becomes spotless white again, and the Bitey by Dusk's side has become two of them without her realizing.

steps.name: Bitey & Bitey?
steps.text: (Tilting their heads at each other)
The two identical Biteys stare each other down for a moment, seemingly confirming the other is the same as them, and then shoulder to shoulder, they happily wander off.
